s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological findings of dense diffuse infiltrate with lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Medical history of well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Ulcer has a clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological examination showed dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo were found in histiocytes and giant cells
Special stains highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

shortlist.label: Oral histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo were found in histiocytes and giant cells, consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Oral cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of intracellular yeasts and granulomatous inflammation, although fungal culture was negative

shortlist.label: Oral blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and histopathological findings, including granulomatous inflammation and intracellular yeasts

shortlist.label: Oral tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation, although no definitive evidence of tuberculosis was found

shortlist.label: Chronic sclerosing sialadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and chronic nature of the ulcer, although not a perfect match for the clinical presentation

rule_in.why: it is most commonly associated with oral ulcers

rule_out.why: it typically presents with salivary gland swelling
